chapters.title: A New Paradigm
chapters.content:
# A New Paradigm

Activitiy DAOs pose as a new class of DAO. Much like a B-Corps, that have a mission that extends beyond traditional fiduciary responsibility to shareholders. Activity DAOs mission is to do the thing, more so than it is to make money for members / donors.

Activity DAOs make sure the DAO gets done, and funding, reputaiton, and incentvies are support structures for achieve this.

Types of DAOs

We can say ActivityDAOs are like a specialized social DAOs.

Additionally we have grouped Grant DAOs within Protocol DAOs which are the most frequent for halving a token or revenue to redistribute to holders.

chapters.title: Maturity Index
chapters.content: # Maturity Index The Activity DAO Maturity Index depicts that natural evolution of how an Activity DAO should evolve. From our times building out BluntDAO we seen different pain poins for each of these different mechanisms and also outlined tools to quickly get started. This is to ensure that a community is more than a community and is resilient to central point of failures and scale. Existing DAOs should be thinking how to embed these systems with in their community to gain further trust in the ecosystem. ActivityDAO Maturity Index

chapters.title: Mechanism Design
chapters.content: # Mechanism Design We will explore the fundamentals of designing an Activity DAO. Unlike traditional DAOs, an Activity DAO's mission is to provide a specific activity as a public good. Every Activity DAO is built on three core elements: organizing the activity, verifying its completion, and funding these activities. These elements combine to create a custom system that proves participation and gamifies reputation and governance within the ecosystem. Understanding the symbiotic relationship between proving the activity, funding it, and governance offers infinite possibilities. We aim to outline mechanisms, share learnings, and provide available tools to facilitate this process. However, this is not its final form.

chapters.title: Proof Mechanism
chapters.content:
# Proof Mechanism Your proof mechanism is a system built on proof of attendance→actvity w/ on-chain referrals via [web of trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_of_trust) to build membership, reputation, that breeds the grounds for how governance & funding around continuing to do the activity. - Recording of the Interaction: This can be facilitated with AI, based on evidence and potential slashing mechanisms. - Onboarding Tracking: You know who onboarded whom. This allows you to: - Incentivize people who bring in active members - Identify those who introduce bad actors - Implement re-up/funding mechanisms to encourage continued participation - Build a reputation system

Advanced systems can include multi-onboarding, where you can reference multiple people you did the activity with, who directly brought you to the activity, and even apply advanced overrides for exact attribution points.

- Slashing: You have a record to audit interactions. Other DAO members could vote to slash or deduct reputation from those who onboard bad actors, even down the dependency tree.

Creating proofing mechanisms may involve entirely different applications. For example, a Pickleball DAO might use [brackets.game](http://brackets.game) as the proof mechanism, taking pictures of winners and determining whether someone competed in, won, or lost a game.   • Initial Attendance: Binary (Attended or Not). Facilitated through Proof of Attendance or Ticketing Applications
